title: Setting up to bake for sale: weigh, test and stay safe
course_title: Basic Baking & Snacks Production: Hands-On Small Batches for Sale

say: Setting up to bake for sale: weigh, test, and stay safe.
This is the video for module 1 of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.
When you bake for sale, every bun must be the same. A cup of flour weighs differently every time, so use a digital scale that reads in 1 g steps.
Put the empty bowl on the scale and press tare, so it shows zero.

panel.heading: Weigh everything on a scale
items: Bowl on the scale, press tare to show 0 g
Add the ingredient slowly to the target weight
Press tare again before the next ingredient
Level small amounts in measuring spoons
Write actual weights on your batch sheet

say: Add the ingredient slowly. Spoon out any extra. Do not pour it back into the bag with a wet spoon.

say: Raising agents lose strength with age, heat and damp, and a flat batch wastes flour, oil and gas. So test them the evening before.
Stir half a teaspoon of baking powder into hot water. It should fizz strongly at once.

cards.d: Half a teaspoon in a few spoons of hot water. It should fizz strongly at once.
A pinch in a spoon of vinegar or lemon juice. It should fizz immediately.
1 teaspoon yeast, 1 teaspoon sugar, about 60 ml lukewarm water. Foam after about 10 minutes.

say: Add a pinch of baking soda to vinegar or lemon juice. It should fizz immediately.

say: Stir 1 teaspoon of yeast and 1 of sugar into about 60 ml of lukewarm water. After about 10 minutes you should see foam. No foam means the yeast is dead.

say: Oven dials are a guide, not a promise. For example, Ngozi in Enugu puts an oven thermometer in the middle of the middle shelf.

panel.heading: Check your oven before you sell
items: Oven thermometer on the middle shelf
Dial at 180, wait 20 minutes: reads 160
Adjust the dial until the thermometer is right
Bread-slice test finds the hot corner

say: She sets the dial to 180 and waits 20 minutes. The thermometer reads 160, so her oven runs about 20 degrees low.

say: Keep the gas cylinder upright, in a ventilated place, away from the burners and out of children's reach.

panel.heading: Gas cylinder and cooker safety
items: Cylinder upright, ventilated, away from heat
Replace a cracked, hard or loose hose
Check joints with soapy water, never a flame
Light ready at the burner before turning the knob
Cylinder valve off at the end of every day

say: To check for a leak, brush soapy water on the joints. Growing bubbles mean gas is escaping. Never test with a flame.

say: Turn the cylinder off every evening.
If you smell gas, do not light anything or touch switches. Turn off the valve if safe, open windows, get everyone out, and call a gas technician or the fire service.

say: Your habits are your promise to customers. Wash your hands with soap for 40 to 60 seconds, and again after raw egg or fish, money, your phone or the toilet.

panel.heading: Personal hygiene
items: Wash hands with soap for 40 to 60 seconds
Wash again after egg, fish, money or phone
Hair covered, clean apron, no jewellery
Cuts covered with a waterproof plaster
No production with diarrhoea or vomiting

say: Cover your hair, wear a clean apron, remove rings, and cover cuts with a waterproof plaster.

panel.heading: Personal hygiene
items: Wash hands with soap for 40 to 60 seconds

say: Do not produce for sale if you have diarrhoea or vomiting. Many food businesses wait until at least 48 hours after symptoms stop.

say: Use the WHO Five Keys as your checklist. Clean with hot soapy water first, then sanitise. Keep raw food apart from finished snacks.
Cook fillings until steaming hot, never leave them out for more than 2 hours, and use treated or boiled water.

panel.heading: The WHO Five Keys
items: Keep clean: clean first, then sanitise
Separate raw fish and egg from finished snacks
Cook fillings until steaming hot
Cooked fillings out no more than 2 hours
Safe water; reject spoiled ingredients

say: To remember. Weigh everything. Store sealed and use the oldest first. Test raising agents. Know your real oven temperature and hot spots. And test gas joints with soapy water only.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Weigh in grams on a tared scale
Store sealed, off the floor, oldest first
Test raising agents before big days
Measure your real oven temperature
Soapy water for gas leaks, never a flame
